assessment.nobel_worthiness: Opened a new observational window: the 2013 detection of a diffuse flux of TeV-PeV astrophysical neutrinos in a cubic-kilometre of Antarctic ice, followed by the 2017 TXS 0506+056 association, NGC 1068 and the 2023 Galactic-plane neutrino map. This is instrument-driven astroparticle physics at its best, with a clear, lasting impact on multi-messenger astronomy and cosmic-ray origin.
assessment.attribution: The supplied credit is a single name. Halzen conceived and led the IceCube concept and its predecessor AMANDA, so he is a defensible sole or principal laureate. As I recall, others (for example early AMANDA/IceCube leaders, or the DUMAND pioneers) have claims; the supplied list cannot settle that and I cannot verify it independently.
assessment.maturity: Strong and increasingly independent: the diffuse flux has been seen in several channels (cascades, tracks, starting events), and source evidence has strengthened over a decade. Timing is good. Source population identification is still incomplete, but the discovery of the flux itself is firm.
uncertainties: Whether a one-person prize is fair given the large collaboration and earlier pioneers.
The sources of most neutrinos remain unidentified, and some source associations are at modest significance.
My knowledge of the detailed credit history is from memory and not independently verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum key distribution turned the no-cloning and measurement-disturbance properties of quantum mechanics into a cryptographic protocol (BB84, and entanglement-based E91). It is conceptually clean, of lasting scientific and practical consequence, and has been realised from lab benches to satellites. Fits well with the committee's recent recognition of quantum information science.
assessment.attribution: BB84 by Bennett and Brassard is the decisive step; Ekert's E91 is an independent and important entanglement-based formulation. A two-person prize is the cleanest; including Ekert would make three but blurs the BB84 priority. Wiesner's earlier conjugate-coding idea is not in the supplied credit, and he cannot receive a prize posthumously, a known allocation problem.
assessment.maturity: Protocol is theoretically mature and demonstrated experimentally many times, including satellite links. Practical security of real devices is a separate active area. Recognition is timely, since the field is decades old and its main players are senior.
uncertainties: Unresolved weight between BB84 and E91 and the role of Wiesner.
Relative to the 2022 entanglement prize, the committee may see overlap.
Quantum information is outside my own expertise, so I rely on colleagues.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, with Katori's magic-wavelength proposal and Ye's demonstration of record accuracy and stability, redefined the frontier of precision measurement and are leading candidates for a redefinition of the second. They enable tests of fundamental physics, relativistic geodesy and searches for dark matter. This is exactly the kind of patient, systematics-driven instrument work I respect.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and built the first clocks; Ye drove the performance to the 10^-18 level and the many-body clock work. Two laureates is a natural configuration. Others in the optical clock field (ion clocks, Hall and Hänsch already recognised for combs) are outside the credit but may be discussed.
assessment.maturity: Multiple independent labs (JILA, RIKEN, PTB, NIST, SYRTE) confirm performance. Timing is good, though a redefinition of the second is still pending, which could make recognition more compelling or merely later.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2005 prize (frequency combs) and possible competing claims from ion-clock groups.
I cannot verify exact priority dates from the supplied text.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices realised Hubbard-type models with exquisite control, from the superfluid-Mott transition to quantum gas microscopes, creating the field of analogue quantum simulation. Original, clearly impactful, and conceptually transparent.
assessment.attribution: Zoller (with Jaksch and Cirac) supplied the theoretical proposal; Bloch and Greiner led the decisive Mott-insulator and microscope experiments. Five credited names make this hard; Cirac, Dalibard and others have legitimate claims, so any three leaves a visible gap. The configuration is not obviously settled.
assessment.maturity: Mature; many groups reproduce and extend the results. Open question is how far the simulations give answers unavailable to classical methods; the foundations are nonetheless secure.
uncertainties: Fair split among five credited people and the Zoller/Cirac pairing.
Overlap with the Bose-Einstein condensation prize of 2001 and with other quantum computing recognition.
Outside my own field, so I would defer to condensed-matter and AMO colleagues.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Measuring the last unknown neutrino mixing angle theta-13 at reactors by antineutrino disappearance showed it to be large, enabling CP-violation searches in the lepton sector. A clean, decisive experimental result of lasting importance, built on careful detector design and systematics control.
assessment.attribution: Daya Bay (Wang, Luk) and RENO (Kim) reported the decisive results in 2012; Double Chooz and T2K contributed to the picture but are not in the supplied credit. Spokesperson-style credit for large collaborations is always debatable, but a three-person configuration is plausible.
assessment.maturity: Very mature: independently confirmed by multiple reactor experiments and accelerator experiments, with precision measurements continuing. Timing is appropriate, though two neutrino-oscillation prizes (2002, 2015) may reduce appetite.
uncertainties: Credit for Double Chooz and accelerator experiments.
Committee fatigue after neutrino oscillation prizes.
Individual attribution within large collaborations.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical readout and coherent control of single nitrogen-vacancy centres in diamond produced room-temperature solid-state quantum sensors for magnetic fields, temperature and biology. A new class of detectors with substantial application reach and a rich basic-physics base.
assessment.attribution: Wrachtrup and Jelezko demonstrated single-NV optical detection and control (1997 onward, with Gruber et al.); Lukin contributed to sensing and quantum-register concepts. The credit is plausible but the NV field has many contributors (Awschalom, Hanson, Budker and others) not in this list.
assessment.maturity: Mature and widely reproduced; applications are emerging. Impact is high, but some parts of the compound (quantum registers, biosensing) may be at different stages.
uncertainties: Competing claims from other groups and overlap with candidate B040.
Whether the prize is about sensing or about solid-state qubits.
Outside my own expertise.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Baryon acoustic oscillations provide a robust standard ruler tying the CMB sound horizon to late-time large-scale structure and underpin precision dark-energy constraints. Clear physical origin, a well-defined measurement, and large cosmological significance.
assessment.attribution: Eisenstein (SDSS LRG) and Cole/Percival (2dFGRS) reported the first detections in 2005. Sunyaev, in the supplied credit, is associated with the theory of acoustic features in the early universe (with Zeldovich/Peebles and Yu in earlier work not listed here), so the theoretical priority is murky. A fair three-person experimental configuration is conceivable but contested.
assessment.maturity: Very mature: confirmed by BOSS, eBOSS, DESI and others. Recent DESI hints of evolving dark energy make the method highly topical but not yet decisive for interpretation.
uncertainties: Theoretical priority (Peebles-Yu, Sunyaev-Zeldovich) is outside the experimental credit.
Cosmology prizes of 2006, 2011 and 2019 may limit appetite.
Large-survey credit across many team members.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: ATLAS and CMS are the detectors that made the Higgs discovery possible and continue to define collider experiment. As a detector builder I place real weight on instrument achievement, with the Charpak (1992) prize as precedent, but the physics discovery itself was recognised in 2013, so the new contribution would be the instruments.
assessment.attribution: The three credited names are the founding spokespersons or conceptual leaders; the contribution of thousands of collaborators and the many subsystem pioneers makes any three-person allocation inherently arbitrary and arguable.
assessment.maturity: Mature and thoroughly validated by a decade of data. Timely in the sense that founders are aging, but a detector-collaboration prize breaks recent patterns.
uncertainties: Whether the committee would credit leadership of a large collaboration rather than specific technical inventions.
Overlap with the 2013 Higgs prize.
Possibly better for a later year.
